And when there was a lull in the gunfire, I moved to my sister-in-law's in the town, that is, to the centre of the town, to Ribarsko neighbourhood, right below the municipal hall.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When the fighting stopped, did you go back to work or did you attempt to go there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: When I came to town, I switched on the radio and I heard them inviting the employees of the KP Dom to come back to work. So I dialled the KP Dom and somebody answered from there and told me not to come.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You said that you switched on the radio and you heard them inviting the employees. When you say "them," whom do you mean? Who was inviting the employees?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: When Foca fell, Radio Foca immediately came on air and there was all sorts of information or, rather, news broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, but who -- could you hear which institution invited the employees of the KP Dom to come back to work?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: It was the Serb Radio Foca.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And to whom did you speak? You said you were told not to come back to the KP Dom. To whom did you speak on the phone?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Micun Jokanovic was the one who took my call. He died meanwhile.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what was his position in the KP Dom at that time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: He was the head of the commercial department.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Before the war?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you hear who was the warden? Was it also broadcast who was the warden? Was it Mr. Tesevic? Did you hear anything in this regard?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No, I did not see Mr. Tesevic, nor did he speak in public, and I heard that Mr. Krnojelac had become the warden and that other institutions -- or, rather, that the war presidency of the municipality of Foca had appointed the managers of -- new managers of all the companies, from Maglic to Kemika [phoen] to the KP Dom, and so on and so forth, the municipal hall, and it was Mr. Mladjenovic who was appointed the chairman of the war presidency of Foca.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When did you hear that Mr. Krnojelac was the warden? Do you know when that was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: It was in late April or mid-April. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Let me clarify. You heard it on the radio or how? Was it announced --

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, yes, on the radio.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And these other persons you just mentioned, the managers of the companies - you also mentioned Mr. Mladjenovic - the new managers, did you know these people?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I knew Mladjenovic personally, because he was the mayor at the time of the war presidency. He taught in the school and later on was appointed the chairman, the president of the war presidency of the municipality of Foca.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: These managers, as you heard it being announced, these managers of the various companies, what ethnicity did they have? Could you say?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Well, I could say, of course. They were all Serbs. They were no Muslims then any more. They had all scattered.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And these new managers, were they involved in politics, would you know?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: One had to be a member of the SDS to be appointed a manager.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Well, because that was the only party -- well, not the only, but it was the strongest party in the Foca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was Mr. Krnojelac a member of the SDS, do you know?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Well, must have been 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you ever see him on political meetings or with politicians before the war?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No, I did not see him with politicians. But since I was not a member of any party, then I went to all the meetings from the SDA, the MBO, that is Muslim Bosniak Organisation, SDS, and so on and so forth. I attended all those meetings because I simply wanted to know what each one of them had to say; that is, I wanted to hear what the views were of party number one, number two, number three, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Krnojelac at such meetings?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: At a stadium of the Sutjeska football club, that is where I did see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when was that, what ...

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: That was before the war --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what time --

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: -- when the parties began to emerge. 1990, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when you saw him, what kind of a meeting was it? Do you know who was assembling?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: That was the founding convention -- or, rather, the election rally of the SDS at the Sutjeska football stadium. They at that time held those rallies at the secondary school, but I did not go there. The only time I was present was at the football stadium.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And where was Mr. Krnojelac when you saw him there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: In front of the stage or, rather, -- yes, in front of the stage. He was up there in the stands.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With whom was he sitting, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I can't really remember, but they were all different men of the SDS, the founders of the SDS party.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Krnojelac together with Mr. Ostojic or Mr. Maksimovic during the war or immediately before the war?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Before the war, yes, not during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when did you see him, and what was he doing?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Walking. Walking in the centre, along the promenade in front of the hotel, and that is the JNA club.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And who was with him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: There were several of them, but I did not know them all that well or, rather, I knew their faces, but not their names.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Vojo Maksimovic, Dr. Vojo Maksimovic was the one I recognised.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what was he wearing, Mr. Krnojelac? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: A suit, no tie.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When were you arrested?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I was arrested on the 10th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When and where did it happen?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: It happened in the centre of the town in my relative's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And who arrested you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Five young men came with rifles. They entered the flat, cocked their weapons, and told me to get ready because they were taking me to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And these young men, were they -- how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: One of them was in a military uniform, and others were half-half, all sorts of things, both civilian and military.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did they tell you where they came from, I mean, from which institution, from which organisation?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: They did not tell me anything. They simply pointed their rifle, their weapons at me and began to go around the rooms and search them.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When they took you away, did they have an arrest warrant or did they have any paper?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No paper. They did not have any paper. The five of them put me on a Peugeot 205, green, no plates, and they put me in the back seat in the middle of two men. No, excuse me, there were four of them. Two sat on each side of me, and two sat in the front. And as they headed for the KP Dom, they said, "Where were you? Where are you? We've been looking for you because there's a warrant for you." And I apologise but I have to say this: I said, "Fuck the one who issued the arrest warrant for me because I know that I did nothing and you're taking me only because I'm a Muslim."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And how did the soldiers -- or the soldiers, yes, respond to this, to your remark?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: They didn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were you ever charged later on during your detention, or convicted?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: When I arrived in the KP Dom, I found there my former colleagues at the gate, at the main entrance. There were some four or five of them, and Mitar Rasevic was one of them, too. As they got out of their car, they all scattered and only the guard and Mitar Rasevic -- the guard who was at the gate and Mitar Rasevic stayed. Mitar Rasevic came to me and said, "What's happened?" Where was I? And I explained where I had been and what had happened, and then he took me into the compound, turned me over to guards, and told them to put me in Room 18.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did he tell you or did anybody else during your detention tell you why you were detained and what the charges against you were?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Up to that time, all the detainees - I mean Muslim and Croats because there were two Croats there, too - up till then they had all been interrogated in the building. And as for me, I spent there about ten months without being interrogated. The guard Milivoje Milic came to Room 18 and called me and another one out, another Muslim, that is, and told us to go to gate 1, that is, told me to take that other one with me because he was disabled, an invalid of some 80, 90 per cent. And he told me to go to Ibro Prohic's office.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what happened in the office?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I entered the office, Ibro Prohic's office. The two of us went in, and there I found Vladicic, Starovic, and Koprivica.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: They were inspectors, police inspectors. Before the war I knew that Vladicic was a police inspector, Starovic was a teacher, and as for that Koprivica, I'm not quite sure what he did before the war. And Koprivica took me into another office, and that was the office used by that social worker, and that other colleague was questioned by Vladicic Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and Starovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And Mr. Koprivica interrogated you, is that what you say?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did he tell you why -- what you were accused of?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No, he did not. He began to ask me where I had been and what I had been doing until the day of my arrest. And he took a typewriter, put it on the desk, put a paper in, and then I began to tell him from the beginning of the war to the day of my arrest where I had been. I told him that I had not been anywhere, that I had been in the town all the time and in the prison, that I had worked in the prison until the outbreak of the war and for three days after the outbreak, and that then I had left my weapon and gone home.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did Mr. Koprivica accuse you of anything in particular? Did he charge you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: In particular, he told me that they had found a radio station with me and that that was the reason why they were bringing charges against me, which is beyond reason. I never had a weapon, let alone a radio station. But the important thing, of course, is to charge you with something, anything. And when all that was over, I signed a statement and went back into the compound.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned that the interrogators, they were -- at least two of them were from the police, from -- in which -- could you find out in which capacity they --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness did not say that at least two were from the police. He said that Vladicic came from police, the second one was a teacher, and he did not know what the third one's profession was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Whereabouts is it? I can't -- my recollection was that there was no particular number of two assigned. Where is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's here, at page 50.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's page 15 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Page 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. 50, sorry. Page 50. And it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Line?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Line 12/18/03. "They were inspectors, police inspectors. Before the war I knew that Vladicic was a police inspector, Starovic was a teacher, and as for that Koprivica, I'm not quite sure."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, then the point is well made.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Well, then you had better reformulate that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Could you make out in which capacity Mr. Koprivica was interrogating you? Did he indicate it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No, he did not tell me, but it was as policemen: Starovic, Koprivica, and Vladicic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Civil policemen or military policemen?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: They had civilian uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Let me return to your arrival in the prison compound. You said that you were taken to Room 18. Why Room 18? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Because building 1 was full and they had begun putting people in building 2. Room 16 was filled to capacity and they began to take people to Room 18 in building 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And who made this decision? Was it Mr. Rasevic, whom you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: He decided that I should be put in Room 18.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: How did he -- being your former colleague, how did he behave towards you when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Strictly -- on strictly official terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And your other colleagues that you met during your detention, how did they behave towards you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Again, strictly officially.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did they --

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Even more than officially; that is, they were rougher than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When you arrived in Room 18, were there other detainees already in this room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: There were, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And were did they come from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Foca, vicinity of Foca. There was a wounded man from Visegrad, from hospital, who was also brought to Room 18.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What was the highest number of detainees in Room 18 that you were with?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Forty-five, fifty.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were those with you in the room, were they all civilians?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: All civilians, down to the last one. Not a single soldier. Even invalids, and that wounded man from Visegrad - I don't know - he was driven out of the hospital and put in the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Room 18?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Some 10 or 15 days maybe, and I was transferred to Room 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: How many detainees were in Room 20 together with you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No sooner did they transfer me or, rather, when they came and told me to move there, I found there 22 men who had been brought from Montenegro, and then more people began to arrive from villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in Room 20?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I stayed there for about a month and then I was transferred to Room 23.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: From Room 23, where was it in the building? On which floor?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Building 2, floor number 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Number 3, you mean -- do you mean the top floor or do you count -- how do you count 3?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: The topmost floor, the last floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Could you see the Drina River from this room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Well, some of it, yes. About half.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show to the witness Exhibit 18, photos 7442 and 7529. Usher, is it possible to put them on the ELMO so that we can see both, that is, the photo 7442 and 7529? Is it possible to place it this way?

utterances.speaker: THE USHER
utterances.text: It's not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's not possible. Okay. We have it, then, one after the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, look at 7442 first and tell us what you see. You have to point out what you see on the ELMO, not on the monitor. It's the other -- the top photo. Yes, this way. Yes. What do you see?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I see a bridge and KP Dom, KP Dom's restaurant and KP Dom's cinema, metal workshop, boiler room, and the top of building 1 and top of building 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Could you please put the pointer on the top of building 1.

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: This section here is a hospital where inmates were in the hospital rooms.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Wait a second. Wait a second.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness was pointing at the building overlooking the administration building left from the trees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It is part of building 1, as the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And it is the portion that comes out from -- in the plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And now continue, please. What do you see -- what do you see on the right side from the trees?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I see a cinema and I can also see room -- building 2 and Room 23, and also a staircase. These are the windows of that room and also the windows of the rehabilitation officer's office.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness was indicating these windows on the right side from the trees.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you tell us which windows are Room 23? If you count them from the left -- from the right side, which windows were to be the windows from Room 23?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: The first one, second one, and then there are two windows that belong to the hallway, and then also one window of the rehabilitation officer's office. This is not a very clear photograph, so I can't really tell.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Then please have a look at the photograph --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you speak into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Please have a look on the photograph 7529. It's a, it's a slightly different -- would you be able to tell which windows you can see from the building 2 next to the trees, which windows would that be?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: The windows of the room that face the compound and Drina River and part of the bridge, and also the windows of the rehabilitation officer's office.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Would you now please look at the photo 7528, that is the -- oh, I had it just the other way around, sorry. Yes, please, the windows, the three windows that you see from the prisoners' quarters, would that be a room, or what would it be?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Well, there were two dormitories there. The lower one faced this side, and the upper one faced the other side.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Dormitories of which room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Twenty-three.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Would the view from these three windows, would it be obscured by the trees or by anything else, or did you have a clear view on to the bridge?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Only -- bridge would be visible only partially, or rather, this part of it on this side was visible.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I didn't see where you were pointing, sir.

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: So the part on the bridge, you're indicating the part on the bridge on the opposite side of the river?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Yes. This was visible from the Room 23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, there was a promise by the Defence before we adjourned at the end of last year that they were going to produce some photographs for this. Have you seen any such photographs?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are we going to be kept in the dark about this, Mr. Bakrac? It may be that you've got photographs from those three rooms which will enable us to see what at least you assert can be seen of this bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the photographs are being developed, and we plan to tender them into evidence through a photographer who produced them on the ground. That is the answer to your question. And the other thing that I wanted to say is, I would like the record to reflect that the witness pointed to the end of the bridge on the other side, and that this is what he had stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: When you say "the other side," you mean the side away from the KP Dom or the --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the opposite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Where he has the -- oh, he's moved it. You mean he's pointed it to this side that we see closest to us in the photograph, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- on the far side of the river?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But may I suggest that if you can speed those photographs up, it would help a great deal because witnesses such as this who would have known the KP Dom very well indeed may be of some assistance to us on it if they can see your photographs as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I shall try after this first recess to bring the photographs after that, but I hope it will be all right with you if I just bring the photographs, the photographs alone; and then later on when we start our case, then we will make an entire photo documentation to present to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That would be very appropriate because as we've pointed out before, the rules in effect require you to show those photographs to witnesses such as the present one. I realise you don't have them here, but it would be very helpful to us if we could get an issue very early in this case as to what you could see from those three windows on the top floor of KP Dom which we can Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. see in this current photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I promise and I take this upon myself to bring those photographs after the first recess.

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: However, a lot can be seen from this photograph as well. One can see from the Room 23 approximately half of the bridge and half of the river.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, I'm sorry to have interrupted you, but I thought if we had the photographs it might help us. I think we're going to have to get some other photograph of this bridge so that we can see what can be seen. Is it only the top of the curved section and, if so, which curved section because there are two as, I recall from one of the earlier photographs that we've seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It may become of some importance in the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's why I wanted to clarify it with the witness who knows the building well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And if you look again on the top photo on this sheet --

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: One can see half of the bridge and half of the river from the Room 23.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Now, you have just indicated on the photo below that the three windows that are not obscured by the trees are Room 23. Now these -- this view shows the trees. Which room would that be that you have said?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Twenty-three, but the living-room section of it, not the dormitory section, because one would enter the living-room section first, and then proceed on to the dormitory section.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's put aside the photos.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would like to put to the witness the floor plan, 6/5. You can use this here.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Would you point out --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Please put it on the ELMO that we can see Room 23 in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Could you point out the windows that you just mentioned? First the windows that were not obscured by trees and then the other three -- the others, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness is pointing at the second room counting from the right side.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Which windows would that be?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: The ones that face the Drina River and the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And those --

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: This is a toilet, this is a second dormitory which faces the upper side, and the rooms -- the two windows in this part face the Drina and the bridge, and then from the living-room section, two windows also face the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But where is the -- what is -- where is it, this section that you call living-room? Could you point out the section you call "living-room"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, may I suggest you ask the witness how many windows in each of these rooms, because the photographs say we can see three windows at the end of the building. That will tell us from which room there was a view of at least a portion of the bridge. You remember that the photograph you've been showing, the description by the investigator as to how she took it does not suggest it was taken from those windows.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You heard the question of the Presiding Judge. Could you tell us beginning from the right side which -- how many windows were in the first room on the right side?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in the second room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: In the living-room section, two.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And following, then, this section where the staircases are, which -- how many windows faced the Drina River? How many windows were there between 23 and 22?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: There were two offices belonging to rehabilitation officers. The one that was in charge of Room 22 had his office, and the one that was in charge of Room 23 had the other office in the hallway.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And how many windows were there facing the Drina?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: One in each. In each office, one.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in Room 22, the section that we're facing directly -- that was following this hall you mentioned, how many windows were there facing the Drina?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, thank you. Witness, the bridge over the Drina, was it big enough for trucks, or was it kind of limited?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Before the war that was the only bridge in town, and it started deteriorating, and it was repaired, a new asphalt was put. And then they put a kind of a border indicating that trucks could not cross this bridge, only passenger vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the river at this point, was it floating slow or fast?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Well, we had a dam in Pluzine, and it all depended on the dam. If the dam worked, then the river would flow noisily, and about -- it produced a lot of noise and cataracts at about 150 to 200 metres. However, if the level in the summer was not so high, then the river would be relatively calm.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned the dam, was it upstream?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Downstream -- no, the dam was upstream.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when it was not operating, when it did not let water through, how was the noise level of the river then?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Well, the noise was less; however, the water level was still good, high.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the weather conditions have an effect on the noise coming from the river?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In which way?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Well, if the level of the water was higher, then the river would swell, then the noise would increase, especially if the snow was melting and there was a lot of rain; however, when the level of the water decreased, then the noise decreased as well. And it was always deep.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in the summer, let's say in April 1992 through to July 1992, how was -- do you recall if the river was noisy or more quiet?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: There were times when it was noisy and there were times when it was quieter, and as I said, it all depended on the dam.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What was the distance between the prisoner quarters and the bridge?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Do you mean from the inmates' building or from the administrative building?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: From the inmates' building.

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: From the building 1, as the Room 13 was closest to the administrative building, then as the crow flies, approximately 100 metres, maybe less. Less, definitely less. I can't tell you exactly. As the crow flies, approximately 20 to 30 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Where in the building did the commander of the guard have his office, in which building, first, and where, on which floor?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Building 1 on the second floor of the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When you say building 1, do you mean the administrative building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Yes, because to the left was the building where the chief of the guard was on the first floor and the chief of the discharge and admittance unit, and on the second floor there was the chief of the rehabilitation unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know if Mr. Rasevic continued to use this office during your detention?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were interrogated in this same building. On which floor were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: On the first floor, in the social worker's office. And across from it was the -- Rasevic's office was across from the office of the chief of the admittance and discharge section.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Rasevic there when you went for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And where was the warden's office before the war? Just the floor.

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: To the right of the entrance to the KP Dom, on the second floor, and again to the right, at the end of the hallway.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And do you know if Mr. Krnojelac used this office during the war, during your detention time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: He did, because on one occasion when they were emptying the register, a secretary of the deputy of the warden was there, as was Savo Todovic. This register was taken down to the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you do it, actually, or how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: The four of us were taken out to carry this register down. This register was -- before the war this register was used by the deputy warden.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what did you see when you were doing this?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I saw the secretary. She was on the same spot where she used to work before. I saw Savo Todovic using the same office as well, but there was a bed in that office now, and as was a stove.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was there a bed in the office of Mr. Todovic or Mr. Krnojelac?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Todovic's office, because we were not allowed -- in fact, there was no need for us to go into the other office as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was Mr. Todovic in the office when you did this job?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Yes, he was, and so was Mitar Rasevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you see Mr. Krnojelac in his office at that time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This secretary that you just mentioned, did she serve the warden and --

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Yes. Starovic, Borkica.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did she serve the warden before the war and also the deputy warden?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did she say anything or did she indicate that she was still doing the same job or ...

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: She was still doing the same job and she was using the same spot she did before the war. And she did not even acknowledge me, despite the fact that before the war we were good acquaintances.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, we heard from other detainees that there were Serb prisoners in the KP Dom. These Serb prisoners in the KP Dom during the war, did you see them and did you know them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Well, they were there and they were in Room 19. However, those were mostly deserters who escaped from the front lines and refused to go to the front. I met a man named Slavko, who killed his girlfriend, who was a Serb. There was also a guy there, a Serb, who was sentenced to 15 years, who attempted to escape across the wall, and he encountered a mine and he was killed. We were having breakfast at the time and it was around 9.30 or 10.00 there. He just happened to be alone in the factory, although that was against the rules. He jumped through the window and started towards the wall; however, there were many mines around the factory and he simply stepped onto one.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were these mines in the prison while you were there as an employee?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No. I don't remember which date it was, but I remember that on that day the lunch was late and the Engineering Unit came in and placed the mines, from gate number 2, across the guards' booths 5, 4, up to the gate 3, all around the wall. Only the guard's booth number 6 was still operating, and that is the guard's booth which is located right next to the administration and close to the building number 1, or rather Room 13, perhaps just 5 metres away from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When you say "Engineer Unit," do you mean a military unit? Was it a military unit doing that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, military unit. They were wearing uniforms, they had helmets, and there were perhaps 12 of them. Because we watched it from across, on the other side. We watched them as they came in.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when was that done? Could you say which month?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: That took place in 1992, June or July.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have mentioned Serb prisoners. Are you able to compare the living conditions of these Serb prisoners and the Muslim detainees? Could you compare, for instance, how the food was for the two groups?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Well, I can only make negative comparisons. Serbs, for example, were allowed visits every day. They were brought in food from home on a daily basis. The food was cooked separately for them and they would go to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. another room, to another hall, to have breakfast, lunch, and dinner. So they were separated from us. Those of us who worked in the factory, we had no contact; we were not allowed contact with them. And that was forbidden for them as well; they were not allowed to have any contact with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you have contacts nevertheless, secretly, or how do you know, then, about their food?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Because we would look through the windows. And after about a year and a half I started working in the factory, so I did have some contacts with them. They worked in the machine unit 1 and we worked in the upholstery department and in other sections of the factory.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned that their food was cooked separately. Did they get more food than the Muslims or the same amount?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Well, there's no comparison there. Before the war we had soup plates, dinner plates, salad plates for the inmates. We purchased it in Belgrade two or three years prior to that. And Radojica was the one who was in charge of that. Before that we used to have plastic plates, which was not really sanitary - they used to crack a lot - and this is why we bought these new plates, and we were given food on salad plates. The meal was given out four times -- well, rather, three times, but the same food was distributed to us four times a day - for lunch, breakfast, dinner - and then the following day we would get the same food for breakfast again. We were never given a can, we were never given meat, nothing fatty at all, and this lasted this way up until the International Red Cross came.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And compared to this limited food that the Muslims got, what did the Serbs get? Are you able to say?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: They were given the same food as us, but they were also given meat and they were given fatty food, because this came out from the common kettle. This was a kettle which was used in Brioni that we in the past used it to boil water, and then they bought it to the KP Dom and they would cook the food together. And once the food was cooked, they would put it in a big pan and take it to the kitchen, where there was a stove, and then they would add fat and meat and cook it some more. But definitely there was a larger quantity of food.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's 11.00 -- sorry, it's 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. We'll resume at 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, were you ever mistreated or beaten while detained in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Well, once I had the chance or, rather, a mischance. We went for lunch, and I entered the rehabilitator's office to take a chair for our room for the Witness 111, and that he needed a chair because he could not sleep and he was learning English. And when I returned from the lunch, Zoran Matovic asked me, "Who took the chair?" And I said "I did," and he locked me up in the solitary confinement. I spent the whole night in the cell until about half past 11. And then Mitar Rasevic came and asked me what happened, and I told him, and then he said to me, "You must not behave like that. Mind your step," and he let me go.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: So Mitar Rasevic, who was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: He was a guard.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when did this happen?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: It happened in July. I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And which year?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And while you were in the isolation cell, were you beaten or hit?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were you alone in the isolation cell, or were there other detainees with you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: In the one that I was in, there was yet another colleague of mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And was he beaten or anyone from the cells next to you, to yours?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No, he was not while I was there. But in the evening at the time of shift change they would go to cells, see who was in those isolation cells, and then they would sometimes beat a Muslim in that cell, because at times they came drunk to take over the night shifts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When you say "they," do you mean -- whom do you mean?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Serbs is whom I mean, guards in the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Could you recall any specific incident so that you can name the victim?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Specifically, Balic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know the first name?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: It eludes me right now, but I know very well that it was the police day, and the brother who was in the police academy in Sarajevo, of the principal of the academy, he congratulated the policeman on that day. I can't remember the date. So the guards came, took him, took him through the gate. He spent there about 15 to 20 minutes, and I saw how they brought him back. He had bruises under his eyes, and they put him in an isolation cell. There he spent some 15 to 20 days, and after that they took him back to his room.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Police day, is that -- which day would that be, from the date?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I think it is sometime in May.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You said you do not recall the first name. In the list we have actually -- in the Schedule B we have actually two different Balices. B-4, that is Dzemo Balic, and B-3, that is Serif Balic.

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Dzemo Balic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Is Dzemo Balic related to Serif Balic? Do you know a Serif Balic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What happened to Mr. Dzemo Balic? Was he --

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: They brought him back to the room, and then they took him to be exchanged, and he never came back.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You say he never came back. Does it mean he -- you don't know what became out [sic] of him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Well, I suppose he was killed, I mean, since he's missing to this day.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you recall when he was taken for exchange and disappeared?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: It all happened in June, July, August, and September 1992. I kept some records in the KP Dom while I was in the Room 18 and 20, and all the others in the room did it with me; but they used to search the rooms, and I was afraid they might find those lists, and I was afraid I might suffer some consequences.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Nevertheless, do you recall any specific incidents where you either saw or heard that a detainee was beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: The most critical times were May, June, July, and August. It was then that they were taking away from 1.500 to 1.700, and they were taking away detainees, beating them, and bringing them back again. I remember Nurko Nisic, who was beaten black and blue and then brought back, but then he was taken away for a second time and did not return.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... second place before we move on to other people you remember, let's first deal with Mr. Nurko Nisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And for the record, Your Honours, it's incident 5.27, described in particular in the indictment, and Schedule C, number 19.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: How often was Nurko Nisic taken out from his room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I know about one occasion when they beat him and a second time when they took him away and after which he did not return.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what did you see when he was taken for the first time and was returned?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I saw bruises under his eyes and I saw that he stumbled.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was he in your room at that time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No. He was in building 1, in Room 15 and 14.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And how did you see him? Where were you and where was he when you saw him with these injuries?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I was in 18 and in the right-hand dormitory. I don't know its number. But I could see exactly, because it was right below that dormitory that he had to go to enter building 1, that is, to go to his room.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And where was he coming from when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Through the gate number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned gate number 1. Which kind of gate do you mean?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: It is the main entrance into the compound of the prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And had you seen him being taken there also or did you only see him return through this door?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: When they took him away, yes, we were at the window, and we waited there for him to come back. And when they did, we were still at the window, so we saw when he was returned. And the second time we saw how he left, but did not see him come back. He just stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was he accompanied by someone when he was taken to the administration building or back?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: There was a guard of the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you recall which guard?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Now, do you remember anyone else in particular, another detainee?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Halid Konjo, Halim Konjo.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Please pause in between. Halid Konjo, who was he and what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: He was also taken away and did not return.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And you mentioned Halim Konjo.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: For the record, he is mentioned in Schedule C, number 13, and Schedule B, number 33.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What did you see happen to Halim Konjo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Halim was also taken away, did not return. And they are two brothers and both were in the restaurant business. Halim was found about five or six kilometres away from Ustikolina. He was found last year.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You said he was found. Does that mean he is alive?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No, no, no. He was found dead. There was an exhumation.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When these two were taken away -- first another question. Did you see them being taken only once or were they also taken several times and returned?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I saw it only once.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when they were taken, especially when Mr. Halim Konjo was taken, did you hear anything afterwards, after he had been taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Halim is the elder of the two. Halid was beaten badly at gate 1, and one could hear them beat him, because he screamed, cried for help. But who beat him, I don't know, and one could not really see who beat him.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This Halim Konjo, did you hear anything in this effect as well from him after he was taken through the gate you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who else do you remember?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I remember Esad Kiselica. He was also taken away and did not come back. Rahman Cankusic --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... pause. Esad Kiselica, that is C-12. Who was he, Esad Kiselica? Who was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Esad Kiselica was an electrician. He worked for Valter Pejic company until about a year before the war, and there he suffered an accident at work and suffered bad burns. He was 80 per cent disabled, barely survived, and he had to change job and moved to office work. He was also taken away. Why, I do not know, but he did not come back and he is still missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you hear the sounds of beating when Mr. Kiselica was taken away?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And you have already started to mention another person. Who was the next person you wanted to mention? You have said Ramo [sic], but then I interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: There was Veiz 1, Veiz 2, Abdurahman Cankusic. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, make a pause when you come to the next person. You said Veiz the one and Veiz the other. Do you know the first names of the Veizes?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: It escapes me right now, but one was a salesman and worked for KTK Visoko shop, and the other one was a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the two Veizes are mentioned under -- Munib Veiz is mentioned under B-59 and C-28, and Zulfo is mentioned under C-29 and the incident 5.27.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, did you -- was any of the Veizes taken on several occasions, or did you see them being taken only once?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I saw it only once, and they did not come back.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you hear the sounds of beating when they were taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, please go to the next person. You mentioned Abdurahman Cankusic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Cankusic, yes. He was also taken away in an unknown direction, that is, through gate 1, and did not come back.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this --

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Islampasic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Just a second, Witness. Your Honour, this is C, Schedule C-3 is Mr. Abdurahman Cankusic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And he's also mentioned, my colleague just told me, he's mentioned also in Schedule B, number 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And you said Mr. Islampasic. What is his first name, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Suad, Suad.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what did you see happen to him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: He also left for exchange and did not come back.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You said he left for exchange, so this has nothing to do, then, with beatings?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: It does not.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when you saw Mr. Cankusic being taken, did you hear beatings afterwards?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Whom else do you remember?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: There were so many of them, I can't remember the names right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have given a statement --

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Aziz Torlak, I've just remembered his name. He was taken away in the morning at half past eight and did not come back.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When was he --

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Allegedly he was taken to be exchanged. He never came back.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And who was he and when was he taken for exchange?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: He was a surgeon, worked in the hospital, and as he was in his white clothes, they brought him from the hospital to the prison. Kemo Tulek, my colleague from the KP Dom, he was brought from Bileca. He was arrested in Kalinovik, transferred to Bileca, from Bileca to Foca. And Milic told me - I just happened to meet him - and he told me that Kemo would not fair well because he was to be court-martialed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Which Milic was that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: A guard in the penitentiary.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know a Ramo Dzendusic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Ramo Dzendusic. He was a clerk responsible for national defence. He was in Room 16, and he was also taken out and away and did not come back. Then there was Mandzo who was a hospital laboratory assistant, can't remember his first name, with Kalaba -- or, rather, his nickname is Kalaba, they both were taken through at gate 1, beaten at gate 1, and brought back to Room 16.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Let me just clarify something. You said you do not know the first name of this Mandzo. Do you know a Salko Mandzo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No, no, it's not Salko. It's not Salko. Salko Mandzo, no, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know a Kelta?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Called Kelta, nickname. That is Salko Mandzo, and his nickname is Kelta.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Let me clarify something. You mentioned a medical person, Mandzo. Is that Kelta or is this --

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- someone else? Who has the nickname Kelta, which Mandzo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Salko Mandzo is Kelta.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Kelta Mandzo is mentioned in B-36 [Realtime transcript read in error "B-26"].

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This Kelta Mandzo, who was he and what did you see happen?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that the witness said that it was not that Mandzo, Salko Mandzo who was beaten, but another Mandzo whose first name he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, the answer at line ten is Salko Mandzo is Kelta.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, 76, 2 and 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We can only go on what he said at line ten. If he said it, then the Prosecution is entitled to accept it. If you want to clear it up, you can do so in cross-examination, if he said two different things.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I refer to lines 2 and 3 when he said that he was not referring to this Mandzo, to Salko Mandzo. And finally, my learned friend referred to an incident which had to do with Salko Mandzo, and now it turns out that the witness was confirming that incident, even though he said that he was not referring to that Salko Mandzo and was not saying that Salko Mandzo, nicknamed Kelta, was the one who had been beaten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Your objection is to the answers he's given, not to the questions which are asked. Now, that's a matter that you can sort out in cross-examination. The Prosecution has asked a question, received an answer, and upon the basis of that answer, pointed out a particular incident in the indictment. There's no confusion in what the Prosecution has done. You will, no doubt, want to suggest that there's been some confusion in the answers. That's a matter for cross-examination. You proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, but I saw that in the transcript there is a mistake. Maybe I misspoke, but it's not B-26, but it's B-36. It's B-36, but let me clarify.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What did you see happen to Kelta Mandzo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Kelta Mandzo has nothing to do with the other Mandzo. Kelta Mandzo just happened to come from work because he worked at the Brioni, and when he reached the gate, they began to beat him. But at that particular moment, Mitar Rasevic came up and said, "Fuck you. That's not the Mandzo. Look for the other Mandzo."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you actually see that or hear it, or did someone -- did Mr. Kelta or someone else tell you about that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Kelta told the story when he came into the room.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you see any injuries on him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I did not see any.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know -- did you see any other Mandzo in the prison?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: The other Mandzo, a lad of some 19, 20 years of age, they were together with that other one, with Kalaba in Room 16, and one of the guards came and called them out, and they went to gate 1. I could see that from Room 18. They beat him for about 15 minutes at gate 1, and then they brought them back to the Room 16 again. And one could see injuries on them, on Mandzo and this young man. He entered the Room 16 with his arcade broken, and Witness 214 sewed up the wound with just a plain needle and thread. In the morning I also went to see the doctor, to our surgery, and I found him there. One could see injuries under his eyes, and the laceration above the eye, and I asked him what happened, and he said, "They took me to the gate with Kalaba and somebody beat me." So I asked him, "Who beat you?" And he said, "I dare not tell you." Subsequently, he also went to be exchanged and did not come back.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we cannot clarify the matter further with this witness, but we think the witness is referring to the incident 5.28, but there's also a Mandzo mentioned in B-37, Emir Mandzo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But is it the same --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But we will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is it the same incident or the same description?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We cannot clarify that further with this witness. It's only that I want to point this out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, this Kalaba you mentioned, what is the correct name of this person?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I can't remember. But this other young man, his name is Emir Mandzo, the one who is a medical technician. He worked at the neuropsychiatric unit. But I don't remember Kalaba's first name. I know, though, that he comes from a settlement which is 6 kilometres away from Foca.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, Your Honour, Emir Mandzo is mentioned under B-37.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, do you know yet another Mandzo, a certain Fuad Mandzo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Fuad Mandzo is yet a third Mandzo. He was in Donje Polje, and they killed Kelta by mistake, and they intended to kill Mandzo Fuad.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You said they killed Kelta. What is that --

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Yes. But when Mitar Rasevic came, they stopped beating him and they let him go. In fact, they were looking for Fuad Mandzo.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: So Kelta wasn't killed?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Fuad Mandzo, Your Honour, is under C-16.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, do you know a person Enes Uzunovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Yes. (redacted). He was also taken away and did not come back.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Uzunovic, in which room was he, and what did you see happen to him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: In Room 18. He was in that room. He was taken out and he did not come back, and allegedly he was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's C-26.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When you say "Room 18," was he together with you in the room? In which room were you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. In 18. I was in that room as well. Because he was initially in Room 11 and then he was transferred to Room 18, from the building 1 to the building 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, do you know a Hamid Bico, nicknamed Salem?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Salem, yes, I knew him as well. He was also taken away to the gate and did not return.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was he taken to the gate only that one time that you just mentioned or did you see him on several occasions?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I saw it once. I also remember Sahinovic. He used to work in a bank. He was taken on several occasions and returned into a room that was sort of a thoroughfare, and he stayed alone in that room. It was in the building 1, next to Room 12. Right to Room 12 was this room that was a passing room, a thoroughfare room, and he was kept there for two or three days. Later on we learned that they beat him because of some money. There was some money involved. His wife was head of the foreign currency unit in the bank, and supposedly 40.000 German marks disappeared.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You refer to Mr. Bico.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: He is mentioned -- Your Honour, he is mentioned in B-5 and C-2.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When he was taken away, did you hear the sound of beating afterwards?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And Mr. Sahinovic is mentioned in the body of the indictment. My colleague is just looking for the specific paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know any person with the last name Rikalo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Rikalo. They were three brothers. They lived in Cohodar Mahala, local commune called Cohodar Mahala. They were in Tivat, from where they were brought to KP Dom. They were also taken away in the afternoon hours, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. after lunch, and they never came back.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just got from my colleague the paragraph in the indictment referring to Mr. Sahinovic, and it's 5.29. And the Rikalo relatives are mentioned in C-21 to 23 and B-45 to 48.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But can you tell us -- yes, please.

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: They are not relatives -- they are not cousins; they're brothers.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And I just wanted to ask you: Do you know their first names?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know an Atko Isanovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Atko was his nickname. His real first name was Adnan. He was in the restaurant business. He had a cafe also in Cohodar Mahala. He was taken away together with six Muslims. This is what I had heard. He was supposedly taken to the hospital to be bandaged, and they were in fact killed near the brook, below the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you hear any sound of beating in relation to this Adnan Isanovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know a person Mensud Pasovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Also known as Pace. I know him as well. He was taken away together with Karabegovic to be exchanged, and he never came back.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When he was taken out, did you hear the sound of beating afterwards?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This person is mentioned under B-44, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know a Kemal Dzelilovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I also know Kemal Dzelilovic. He was also taken away. I saw him being taken away in the afternoon hours. He was taken to the gate, where he was beaten, and then he was returned. When they took him away for the second time, he did not return after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is C-7, Schedule C, number 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you see injuries on him when he was returned for the first time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I did, for the first time, yes. I saw bruises under his eyes, both eyes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And which time passed between his being taken for the first time and then for the second time when he disappeared? How much time passed between the two times?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: The following day. This is how it usually happened: In the afternoon they would beat somebody and then the following day they would take them away, although sometimes it happened on the same day. They were taking people away usually between 3.30 in the afternoon till about 7.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when you say "they," whom do you mean?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I mean Serbs. Guards would come, call out names, and take out people to the gate 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know a Krunoslav Marinovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Certainly. I know him as well. He used to work as a TV repairman. He was married to a Serb with maiden name Gagovic who worked in the military office. He was also taken away and he did not return. Zulka, known as Zoran, medical technician, worked at the ear, nose, and throat unit. He was in prison twice. The first time they released him. The second time when they took him he did not return. He was married to a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This Zoran -- but this Zoran has nothing to do with Mr. Krunoslav Marinovic, or --

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: No. I only mention it together because those were two Croats, the only two Croats in the KP Dom, and this is why I linked them.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Marinovic is under C-17.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You said Zoran, a Croat. Would you know the last name?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I can't remember. A long time went by, so I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know Juso Dzamalija?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Juso Dzamalija was an older man. He lived in Sukovac, where he had a house. That was across from the KP Dom. He was about 65 to 70 years old. He was also taken away and did not return.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When was he taken away, and did you hear afterwards any information about what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Well, I didn't. We didn't know what happened. And if somebody did not return, that meant that they were killed. This was our reasoning. If somebody was taken for exchange or for other purposes, this is how we reasoned. We couldn't see what else could have happened to them other than being killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This person, Juso Dzamalija, is under C-6.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, you have already mentioned several times now that they were taken into this door, into the administration building, and were beaten. Could you hear from the sounds in which part of the administration building those people were beaten? Could you make it out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Room 13 could hear it, 11, 16, and 18.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... misunderstanding. I was asking -- I wanted to know: Could you make out from which part of the administration building the sound of beating and the screams came from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: It would usually come from gate 1 or from the so-called passing room, a thoroughfare room which was behind the place where officers on duty were.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to put in front of the witness Exhibit 61A.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, if you look at the floor plan of the administration building, could you show us where this passing room is?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: This is an entrance. To the left was the office where officers on duty were, and then next to it was this passing room, or through room. It had grates on the windows and it had concrete on the floor and it had two big rings on the floor which were attached to the concrete on the floor. We created this room before the war so that if some prisoners came drunk, we would normally put them in this room to sober up and then in the morning release them. So the screams were heard from this room. We could hear the sounds from this room.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Would you please point at this spot and leave it there.

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness is pointing at the fourth room from the left side in the administration building, facing the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you hear the sounds of beatings coming from this room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: Yes. That could be heard in Room 13, in Room 13, and also the Room 11 could hear sounds from this room. We in Rooms 16 and 18 could hear sounds from the gate 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Would you point at the spot in this sketch where you could hear screams coming from.

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: I could hear it from Room 18.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, but from where did you hear the sounds come from, the sounds of beating?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: From gate 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness was pointing at the entrance of the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Could you put it -- the pointer right on the spot and leave it there.

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
utterances.text: This is gate 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And that's the entrance, actually, to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-138
